title: Block sliding to a stop on a rigid wall with Coulomb friction (explicit)
source: A rigid block launched at v₀ on a horizontal plane with Coulomb friction μ decelerates at μg and stops after v₀/(μg) at v₀²/(2μg), its kinetic energy all dissipated by friction; Meriam & Kraige, Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics, §3/5 (work and energy)

quantities.quantity: distance travelled (top centre node) against v₀²/(2μg) = 1.5
quantities.reason: the wall's friction impulses are exact Coulomb impulses; the block's elastic vibration from the sudden gravity and the friction moment move the node by a fraction of a percent

quantities.quantity: velocity of the top centre node after the stop
quantities.reason: the block sticks; what is left is its elastic vibration, under 1% of v₀
the kinetic energy goes into friction; the vibration and the work of gravity as the block settles add or take a fraction of a percent
